title: ALGORITHMIC FAIRNESS IN AI SURROGATES FOR END-OF-LIFE DECISION-MAKING
reasoning: The paper explicitly explores algorithmic fairness through the lens of various moral and religious traditions, including Western bioethics, Confucianism (ren, li), Islamic ethics (adl, rahmah, shura), Hindu and Buddhist traditions (dharma, karuna, ahimsa), and Indigenous ethics (CARE principles). It evaluates how these spiritual and philosophical frameworks should inform the design and deployment of AI systems in end-of-life care.
